preconditions.description: The number of people n is between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(parents) == n and all(0 <= p <= n for p in parents)
preconditions.description: The parent list contains exactly n integers, each being 0 or a valid person index between 1 and n.
The number of queries m is between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(queries) == m and all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= p <= n for v, p in queries)
preconditions.description: There are exactly m queries, each consisting of a person index v and a depth p, both within valid ranges.
The family relationships defined by parents do not form cycles (guaranteed by problem statement).

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly m integers, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(ans, int) for ans in output_list)
postconditions.description: Each answer in the output is an integer.

postconditions.expression: all(count_pth_cousins(v, p, parents) == output_list[i] for i, (v, p) in enumerate(queries))
postconditions.description: For each query i with person v and depth p, the i-th output integer equals the count of p-th cousins of v. A p-th cousin of v is a person y (y != v) such that there exists a person z who is a p-ancestor of both v and y.
